content.text: w/ normal life expectancy & performance status,
no change in proportions of HbA, HbA2, & HbF, just lower amounts
: in presence of reduced alpha chains, excess β chains are unstable & precipitate, causing damage to RBC
membranes which leads to intramedullary (bone marrow) & peripheral blood hemolysis
jaundice & anemia at birth, pallor & splenomegaly
during periods of erythropoietic stress (e.g., infection, pregnancy)
: intrauterine ascites & hydrops fetalis, severe splenomegaly, cardiac & skeletal abnormalities
death in utero or shortly after birth
folic acid supplementation during periods of erythropoietic stress (e.g., pregnancy, acute infections)
: reduced β-globin chain synthesis results in a relative ⇡ in proportions of HbA2 & HbF compared to HbA as the β-like globins (δ & γ) substitute for the missing β chains
during periods of erythropoietic stress +/- iron
infants protected by HbF up to 6mo of age
, after which HbF production ⇣ & severe anemia develops
: Hgb electrophoresis, high performance liquid chromatography
folic acid supplementation during periods of erythropoietic stress (e.g., pregnancy, acute infections)
transfusion therapy q2-5wks to keep Hgb >9-10g/dL
